title: Neutral assignment-scope description: core stops reading Scopes internals (D21)
summary: Adds core `Contracts\Scopes\DescribesAssignmentScope` and `Context\AssignmentScopeDescription` (D21, knowledge/p3-execution#scope-description), implements them in the module's `BaseAssignmentScope`, and rewrites every core reader of `Scopes\Internal\ScopeConfiguration`, `BaseAssignmentScope`, `RoleBindings` and `ConfigurableAssignmentScopeDefinition` (PanelCompiler, PanelFingerprint, RoleCompiler, ResourceContextMapping, BatchInputs, SchemaBuilder) to use the description; same-alias definitions become identical-or-conflict; ScopesPlugin validates its own options. Files stay where they are (relocation is P3.4).
why: After the relocation core must reference no module type (I2), yet P2 left core reading module facts through interim readers (P2.7/P2.8/P2.10 deviations). Hard risks: the description must reproduce every fact exactly (tenant-owner rejection, filters-without-evaluator rejection, batched resolution only for the base resolver, owner inline read) — a wrong `resolvesThroughQuery` or `tenantOwner` silently changes scalar/batch/SQL agreement (I9) or tenant isolation; fingerprints must still change when a filter, membership or adapter changes, or a stale catalog cache would be trusted.

include: New `AzGuard\Contracts\Scopes\DescribesAssignmentScope` and `AzGuard\Context\AssignmentScopeDescription` exactly as knowledge/p3-execution#scope-description; oracle rows for both added by the #oracle procedure

`AzGuard\Scopes\BaseAssignmentScope` implements `DescribesAssignmentScope` (`components` = settings filters, label, directory, `resolvesThroughQuery` by the reflection rule); `AzGuard\Scopes\ModelAssignmentScopeDefinition` reports `tenantOwner` = `hasOwner()`

Core call sites rewritten per the #scope-description table: `Panels\PanelCompiler` (tenant owner, filters without evaluator, identical-or-conflict instead of `sameStructure`/`merge`, alias default directory), `Panels\PanelFingerprint`, `Catalog\RoleCompiler`, `Authorization\Internal\Query\ResourceContextMapping`, `Authorization\BatchInputs`, `Schema\SchemaBuilder` (core enumeration of `BaseRole::scopes()`, `exactSupport` per #amendments)

`AzGuard\Scopes\ScopesPlugin::register()` validates its options (adapter alias ⊆ own definitions, membership/adapter contract) and `Scopes\Internal\Checks\ScopeMembershipConfigured` reports container-unresolvable membership/adapters as error findings; `Scopes\Internal\ScopeConfiguration` keeps only module-internal helpers
`Schema\AssignmentScopeBindingSchema` docblock of `$exactSupport` updated; i2.json entries of `BatchInputs.php` and `SchemaBuilder.php` removed

Migration lines: same-alias contributions with different filters/label/directory now conflict; `exact_support` is false for adapter-backed types; a custom definition implements `DescribesAssignmentScope` to give core label/directory/owner facts
exclude: Moving files into module roots or changing module FQCNs (P3.4)
Any change of scope semantics beyond the listed rules

reads.why: Rules every P3 item follows (reference + amendments win, no shims, placement, oracle, allowlists, snapshots, migration lines, tests)
Exact validation commands, PHP 8.4, driver ports, composer update rule
Which allowlist entries this item removes

Procedure to add the two new rows to the ownership oracle

Existing scope contracts the new capability extends

rules: After this item no file under packages/core/src outside src/Scopes, src/Audit, src/Plugins/Audit, src/Contracts/Scopes and src/Directories/QueryScopeDirectory.php references `AzGuard\Scopes\` other than `Scopes\Query\{PredicateBuilder,PredicateQuery,QueryGuard}` (moved by P3.4).
Error messages and exception classes of the replaced checks stay byte-identical (tests assert them).

Negative tests: a tenant-required panel with an ownerless model definition; filters without evaluator (panel and role binding); two different same-alias contributions conflict; a custom resolve() is not batched and not inlined; changed filter/membership/adapter changes the fingerprint.
guidance: Implement the description helper for non-implementing definitions in an existing core class (rule 5); do not add a helper type. Run the #oracle procedure before the first test run, otherwise OwnershipScanTest fails on the two new files.
